cues.en: So now that we have seen how file system checks work, let's now have a look at how we can automatically
run those file system checks.
Um, you could also enable automatically checking.
So by default Ubuntu is configured in a way that it does not automatically check the file systems on
boot.
By default, it will only check the file system when a so-called dirty bit has been set and that usually
gets set if the drive would shut down at an unexpected power loss.
Uh, in that case ubuntu should check the file system during next boot.
So this means that for example, um, the volume has not been unmounted properly.
Um, we can prevent this in the last column in the etcd tab if we have a look at that one, I could
edit the etcd fstab and if I edit this file we can see here the last column.

important than data.
Integrity might be a judgment call that we might do, and then we could set this to zero.

properly or there was a power outage and it failed while writing some data to the disk, we don't do
the file check at all.
